Former Manchester United midfielder, Paul Ince, has urged the club to prioritise Ollie Watkins or Ivan Toney over Nigerian striker Victor Osimhen, as they search for a “25-goal man” to lead their attack. Ince, who spoke to GOAL in association with freebets.com, said United have lacked a reliable out-and-out striker for years. He said he liked Osimhen, having watched him a lot in Turkey this year, but felt two other players were better options. “Go and get Ivan Toney or go and get Ollie Watkins. Both proven Premier League players. I know they are playing in Saudi for a sack full of money, but if you are looking for out-and-out strikers who are proven in the Premier League, go and get Ollie Watkins or Ivan Toney, someone like that, because they do create chances. Manchester United have created so many chances this season. They just cannot find the back of the net,” he said. United have struggled to replace the days of Andy Cole, Dwight Yorke, Ruud van Nistelrooy, Wayne Rooney and Robin van Persie. Rasmus Hojlund cost £72m but scored 26 goals in two seasons and is now at Napoli. Benjamin Sesko joined for £74m in 2025 and scored 12 goals in his first campaign, many of them as a substitute. Bassey hands Devils boost as Fulham set huge price Pochettino arrives at Man United ahead of Liverpool clash EPL: Panel identifies six refereeing errors in one weekend Ince said the 23-year-old may see himself as a super sub. “Every time he started, he never really seemed to do it. Maybe he looked at himself as more of a super sub than actually starting the game,” he said. He also criticised the way the squad had been built. “Now, what you have done, you have brought in Cunha, you have brought in Mbeumo, and it is like, where do I play them? They have never really gone and said, ‘we need to find that 20, 25-goal man who is going to score those goals’.” He added that United’s defensive problems made goals more important. “Villa scoring four at Old Trafford, that is never been heard of. Teams do not come to Old Trafford and score four goals. Bournemouth came to Old Trafford and scored three goals. That is unheard of. And if they are not scoring goals themselves, this is the product you get from these games. And this is why you find them third from bottom.” Mauricio Pochettino inherits a team in the relegation zone after Michael Carrick was sacked, and his first game will be at Liverpool on Sunday.
